title: Stochastic Gates for Covariate Selection in Population Pharmacokinetics Modeling

content.abstract_summary: Proposes Stochastic Gates (SG), an embedded neural network feature selection method, for automated covariate prescreening in population pharmacokinetics. Unlike wrapped approaches (SHAP + XGBoost), SG simultaneously trains the model and selects covariates via a penalized gate layer — eliminating the need for post-hoc feature removal and separate retraining. Evaluated on synthetic datasets (correlated covariates, low-frequency categorical, high IIV, small population, XOR nonlinear dependency) and on two clinical datasets: monalizumab (507 subjects) and tixagevimab/cilgavimab (4940 participants). From AstraZeneca (Barcelona/Cambridge/Gaithersburg/Waltham), published in the WG's target journal CPT:PSP.
key_findings: Stochastic Gates exactly match expert-identified covariates for monalizumab CL (BWT, BALB) and Vc (BWT, BALB, SMK, SEX) — demonstrates ML covariate prescreening can achieve expert-level accuracy on a real industry dataset

For tixagevimab/cilgavimab, SG identifies a superset of expert covariates (all expert covariates included plus additional ones) — backward elimination recommended after SG prescreening; XGBoost identifies fewer spurious covariates than BorutaShap but more than SG
SG outperforms XGBoost/BorutaShap specifically for highly correlated covariates — correctly identifies BWT (not correlated BBSA) in reference scenario where XGBoost cannot distinguish them

Warm start capability: initializing μ-gate parameters for preferred covariates allows domain knowledge priors to influence selection — useful when biologically meaningful and synthetic covariates are linearly dependent (data cannot distinguish them alone)
XOR nonlinear covariate dependency successfully recovered — key advantage of ML over linear SCM; stepwise approaches cannot detect nonlinear covariate interactions
Limitation explicitly flagged: SG relies on EBE, which can be biased under high shrinkage; peripheral compartment parameters with >30% shrinkage excluded from analysis
limitations: SG relies on EBE which is biased under high shrinkage (>30%) — peripheral compartment parameters must be excluded, limiting scope to identifiable parameters
Does not specify the functional form of covariate-parameter relationships; visual inspection (SHAP, symbolic regression) is still needed after covariate selection
High IIV (120% CV) narrows the range of penalty hyperparameter λ over which correct covariate selection occurs — fine-tuning becomes harder
Small populations (N=100) cause overfitting; only medium-effect covariates (30% effect size) reliably found
Covariate 'leakage' across PK parameters when correlations between random effects are high (>40%) — backward elimination step required

extracted_claims.text: For monalizumab, the covariates found on clearance and volume of distribution corresponded exactly to the covariates found by the expert.

This machine learning-based method enhances the covariate preselection process in population pharmacokinetics model development, offering significant time savings and improving efficiency even under challenging scenarios.

numerical_findings.description: Monalizumab clinical dataset size (pooled from 2 studies)
Tixagevimab/cilgavimab clinical dataset size (pooled from 8 clinical trials)

gaps_addressed: Directly fills M1.3 (ML for covariate selection in pop PK) — the dominant practical use of ML in industry pharmacometrics; provides a state-of-the-art embedded method that outperforms wrapped SHAP/XGBoost approaches for correlated and nonlinear covariate effects
The XOR scenario result is a key argument for ML in the WG scoping paper: standard SCM/LASSO cannot detect nonlinear covariate interactions that neural networks recover

provenance.notes: Found via PubMed search 'machine learning covariate selection population pharmacokinetics' (PMID 41637692). PMC12872115 (open access). CPT:PSP 2026, 15(2):e70147. AstraZeneca (all authors). Industry-funded. All authors are or were AstraZeneca employees. Retrieved full text via PMC. The 'warm start for preferred covariates' capability is a novel contribution not available in XGBoost/SHAP approaches and would be useful when WG needs to prioritize physiologically interpretable covariates over correlated alternatives.
